parole.significato: ginger
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi अदरकी (adarkī) / Urdu اَدْرَکِی (adrakī)), from अदरक (adrak, “ginger”) + -ई (-ī) / اَدْرَک (adrak, “ginger”) + ـِی (-ī), from Prakrit *𑀆𑀤𑁆𑀤𑀅 (*āddaa), in turn from Sanskrit आर्द्रक (ārdraka, “ginger”), ultimately from आर्द्र (ārdra, “wet”), as fresh ginger is wet. parole.significato: A landholder in possession of a bhag.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi भागदार (bhāgdār), Urdu بَھاگْدَار (bhāgdār)); of which the first element भाग (bhāg) / بَھاگ (bhāg) is derived from Sanskrit भाग (bhāga, “part, share, piece”), and the second one -दार (-dār) / ـدَار (-dār) is a suffix derived from Classical Persian ـدَار (-dār, “holder

parole.significato: Indian: of, or relating to, the Republic of India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi भारतीय (bhāratīya), भारती (bhāratī) / Urdu بھارتی (bhāratī)). By surface analysis, Bharat + -i.

parole.significato: A spiced dish of rice, blended with meat and/or vegetables.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi बिरयानी (biryānī) / Urdu بِرْیَانی (biryānī)), from Classical Persian بِرْیَانِی (biryānī), from بِرْیَان (biryān, “roast”) (from برشتن (birištan, “to roast”)) + the suffix ـی (-ī). Doublet of briam.

parole.significato: An enveloping Central Asian garment which covers the whole body, incorporating a netted screen to cover the eyes, chief…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi बुरक़ा (burqā) / Urdu بُرْقَع (burqa')), from Classical Persian بُرْقَع (burqa'), from Arabic بُرْقُع (burquʕ).

parole.significato: An honoured elder or superior.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi बुज़ुर्ग (buzurg) / Urdu بُزُرْگ (buzurg), from Classical Persian بُزُرْگ (buzurg), from Middle Persian 𐭥𐭰𐭥𐭫𐭢 (wazurg, wuzurg), from Old Persian 𐎺𐏀𐎼𐎣 (vazạrka, “great, large”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wáȷ́rakas (“endowed with strength”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Eu

parole.significato: A sycophant and hanger-on or lackey.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi चमचा (camcā) / Urdu چَمْچَہ (camca, “yesman, sycophant, hanger-on, lackey, pet, puppet, stooge”, literally “spoon”)), from Classical Persian چَمْچَه (čamča), from Turkic, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kamïč,.

parole.significato: A screen or blind made of finely slit bamboo and twine, hung in doorways or windows.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi चिक़ (ciq) / Urdu چق (ciq)), ultimately from Classical Persian چق (čiq).

parole.significato: An oriental plane tree (Platanus orientalis).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi चिनार (cinār) / Urdu چِنَار (cinār), in turn derived from Classical Persian چِنَار (činār, “Platanus”), ultimately derived from Middle Persian cynʾl (/⁠činār⁠/).

parole.significato: An unskilled Asian worker, usually of Chinese or Indian descent; a labourer; a porter. Coolies were frequently transpor…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi क़ुली (qulī) / Urdu قلی (qulī, “hired laborer”)), from Chagatai قلی (quli, “servant, slave”), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kul. Another theory says that it is named after Gujarati કોળી (koḷī), a Gujarati tribe or caste. Other forms occur in Bengali কুলি (kuli) and Ta

parole.significato: A yogurt or fermented milk product.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi दही (dahī) / Urdu دَہِی (dahī)), from Old Hindi दही (dahī), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀳𑀺 (dahi) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), ultimately from Sanskrit दधि (dádhi). Doublet of tyre.

parole.significato: a drum having two heads opposite one another, commonly used in the Hindu and Buddhist religions.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi डमरू (ḍamrū) / Urdu ڈَمَرُو (ḍamarū)), Sanskrit डमरु (ḍamaru) and Tibetan ཌ་མ་རུ (ḍa ma ru).

parole.significato: A double layer of cloth worn by women as a scarf, veil etc.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi दुपट्टा (dupaṭṭā) / Urdu دُوپَٹَّہ (dūpaṭṭa)).

parole.significato: cardamom
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi इलायची (ilāycī) / Urdu اِلائِچی (ilāicī)), from Middle Hindi, from Old Hindi, from Sauraseni Prakrit, from Prakrit, ultimately from Proto-South Dravidian *ēlVkkāy. Related to Sanskrit एलीका (elīkā), Classical Persian هیل (hēl).

parole.significato: Pertaining to a fair-skinned or European person.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani Hindi गोरा (gorā) / Urdu گورا (gorā). * In British Pakistani speech, influenced also by Pahari-Potwari گورا (gorā) and Punjabi ਗੋਰਾ (gorā) / گورا (gorā).

parole.significato: An assignment of the produce and income of a particular district or village to a person or persons, as an annuity
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi जागीर (jāgīr) / Urdu جَاگِیر (jāgīr)), from Classical Persian جَاگِیر (jāgīr, “jagir”), from جَا (jā, “place”) + گِیر (gīr), the present stem of گرفتن (giriftan, “to take”).

parole.significato: One who holds a jagir.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi जागीरदार (jāgīrdār) / Urdu جَاگِير دَار), from Classical Persian جَاگِير دَار (“jagirdar”).

parole.significato: a kind of duet in Indian classical music.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi जुगलबंदी (jugalbandī) / Urdu) and/or Bengali যুগলবন্ধী (juglobondhi).

parole.significato: A large, lush, undeveloped, humid forest, especially in a tropical region, thick with vegetation and wildlife; a tropic…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi जंगल (jaṅgal) / Urdu جَن٘گَل (jaṅgal)), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀚𑀁𑀕𑀮 (jaṃgala), from Sanskrit जङ्गल (jaṅgala, “arid or sterile region, desert”), from a substrate language. First appears c. 1776 in a translation by Nathaniel Halhed.

parole.significato: Chiefly preceded by in or on: the state each year during which a male animal (usually a camel or an elephant) exhibits…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi मस्त (mast) / Urdu مَسْت (mast, “drunk, intoxicated; lustful”); and also from Middle Hindi مَسْت (mst /⁠mast⁠/)), and from its etymon Classical Persian مَسْت (mast, “(adjective) drunk, intoxicated; (literary) in rut; of an elephant: in musth; (noun) drunkard”), ultima

parole.significato: A dance in the Indian subcontinent, performed by professional dancing girls.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi नाच (nāc) / Urdu ناچ (nāc)), in turn derived from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀡𑀘𑁆𑀘 (ṇacca), ultimately derived from Sanskrit नृत्य (nṛtya), which was originally नृत्त (nṛttá) (also see नृत्यति (nṛtyati, “to dance”)).

parole.significato: A South Asian stew of slow-cooked beef or lamb with bone marrow.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi निहारी (nihārī), नहारी (nahārī) / Urdu نَہَارِی (nahārī)), from Classical Persian نهاری (nahārī, “breakfast”), from Arabic نهار (nahār, “daytime, day”).

parole.significato: Clothes for wearing to bed and sleeping in, usually consisting of a loose-fitting shirt and pants/trousers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi पाजामा (pājāmā) / Urdu پاجامہ (pājāma)), from Classical Persian پَاجَامَه (pājāma, “trousers, drawers”), from پَا (pā, “leg”) + جَامَه (jāma, “garment”).

parole.significato: A workman who repairs shawls and other woolen fabrics; a darner.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi रफ़ूगर (rafūgar) / Urdu رفوگر (rafūgar) / رفو گر (rafū-gar)), in turn derived from Classical Persian رفوگر (rafūgar).

parole.significato: A provider of financial services in the Middle East and in South Asia, especially (historical) during the early modern…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi सर्राफ़ (sarrāf) / Urdu صَرَّاف (sarrāf) and Classical Persian صَرَّاف (sarrāf), from Arabic صَرَّاف (ṣarrāf).

parole.significato: A square or rectangular piece of cloth worn as a covering for the head, neck, and shoulders, typically by women.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi शाल (śāl) / Urdu شال (śāl)), from Classical Persian شال (šāl). Doublet of sari through Sanskrit.

parole.significato: A provider of financial services, especially a small-scale independent banker or money changer or (historical) a local…
parole.testo: An British Indian variant of saraf, borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi सर्राफ़ (sarrāf) / Urdu صَرَّاف (sarrāf) and Classical Persian صَرَّاف (sarrāf), from Arabic صَرَّاف (ṣarrāf).

parole.significato: A professional courtesan serving the nobility, especially under the Mughal Empire; (derogatory)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi तवायफ़ (tavāyaf) / Urdu طَوائِف (tavāif)), in turn derived from Classical Persian طَوَائِف (tawā'if), ultimately derived from Arabic طَوائِف (ṭawāʔif).
